definitions.explanation: The dot separating the whole-number part of a figure from its fractional part. Japanese uses the same period as English, and positions after it are counted with {位|くらい} (place).

examples.japanese: {小数点|しょうすうてん}を{忘|わす}れた。
{小数点以下|しょうすうてんいか}は{切|き}り{捨|す}ててください。
examples.english: Please drop everything after the decimal point.

examples.japanese: {小数点|しょうすうてん}を{一|ひと}つ{間違|まちが}えただけで、{金額|きんがく}が{十倍|じゅうばい}になってしまった。
examples.english: Just one mistake with the decimal point made the amount ten times larger.

notes:
From {小数|しょうすう} (decimal fraction) plus {点|てん} (dot). Digits after the point are counted as {小数点|しょうすうてん}{第一位|だいいちい}, {第二位|だいにい}, and so on.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小数点以下|しょうすうてんいか}: below the decimal point; the fractional part
- {小数点|しょうすうてん}{第二位|だいにい}まで: to two decimal places
- {小数点|しょうすうてん}を{打|う}つ: to put in a decimal point
- {小数点|しょうすうてん}をずらす: to shift the decimal point

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {整数|せいすう}: whole number, integer — what sits to the left of the point
- {分数|ぶんすう}: fraction — the other way of writing a non-whole number, with a numerator and denominator
